text:
tim: quick heads-up — ran a production soak on the batch-bridge connector and observed sustained queue growth for a few minutes. threshold crossings cluster around 8–12ms. not a full outage but latency tails spiking. anyone recall any contract changes recently?

jess: can you dump the last 30s of metrics and the bridge logs?

tim: pasted: <grafana://redwood/bridge/p99>. here's the snippet from the bridge: 
```
2026-03-18T15:02:10Z bridge.go:341 WARN enqueue delay=9.8ms headroom=-1.2 tokens=0
2026-03-18T15:02:11Z coalesce.go:88 INFO batch emitted size=12 latency=11.4ms
2026-03-18T15:02:13Z bridge.go:345 DEBUG dequeue wait=7.1ms backpressure=soft
```

sri: two quick hypotheses: 1) sampling bias: our telemetry only reports when a batch crosses emit barrier so we miss short-lived reconvergence, 2) contract loosened when we added peek semantics last quarter (peek lets coalescer examine head without decrementing tokens). both could raise observed thresholds.

omar: +1 on peek. peek was added to let runtime decide reorder without consuming KV head — but if coalescer peeks and then defers, bridge still counts the request as active which reduces effective headroom.

jess: if peek is causing the bridge to treat a request as live, we should distinguish states: PEEKED vs RESERVED. Maybe bridge should allocate a "soft token" for peek and only convert to a hard token on reserve.

tim: that feels right. current proto between queue and bridge is minimal. re: interface, proposal below: 
```
service BridgeQueue {
  rpc Enqueue(EnqueueReq) returns (EnqueueResp);
  rpc Peek(PeekReq) returns (PeekResp); // non-consuming, gives visibility
  rpc Reserve(ReserveReq) returns (ReserveResp); // turns peek->reserved or enqueue->reserved
  rpc Release(ReleaseReq) returns (ReleaseResp);
}
message EnqueueResp { string ticket_id = 1; }
message PeekResp { string ticket_id = 1; bool had_payload = 2; }
```

sri: love the explicit states. tradeoffs: more RPCs and bookkeeping, slightly higher headroom bookkeeping cost, but prevents double-counting. Also need timeouts: Peek should auto-expire after X ms to prevent leaked soft tokens.

omar: operational note — if we add soft tokens, metrics must report both soft and hard headroom. otherwise SLO math breaks for autoscaler and admission.

jess: agree. also want to test two failure modes: 1) coalescer crashes after peek but before reserve (should auto-release soft token), 2) network partition where reserve ack is lost — need idempotent Reserve and idempotent Release paths.

tim: I'll sketch a follow-up RFC with: state machine (ENQUEUED -> PEEKED -> RESERVED -> COMPLETED/RELEASED), soft-token TTLs, metric flavors (soft_tokens, hard_tokens), and a backwards-compatible fallback that treats Peek as Reserve for old bridges.

deploy-bot: note: rolling canary of bridge v2 starts at 2026-03-19T04:00Z — will include TTLs by default=false.

sri: test plan: small canary with synthetic microburst, enable soft-token path and observe p99 and queue-size differences. capture traces with span tags: bridge.state and token.type.

jess: one more thought — consider exposing a "hint" in PeekResp that suggests coalescer urgency (low/medium/high). bridge could use hint to prioritize eviction. cheap and might reduce tail.

tim: good call. I'll add hint:enum { LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH } to PeekResp and add to RFC. thanks all — i'll post RFC draft tomorrow and tag for eng-runtime review.
